function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a “starter kit” – i.e. a quick‑reference cheat sheet – for anyone who wants to expose or consume a **Startup Statistics API**.  
It covers:

| What you’ll see | Why it matters |
|-----------------|---------------|
| Base URL & version | Keeps clients stable even when new features arrive |
| Authentication scheme | Protects private data while letting developers sign up easily |
| Core resources (`startup`, `investment`, `valuation`) | Gives you everything you need to describe a company’s life cycle |
| Common query params (`q`, `page`, `per_page`, `sort_by`) | Lets users filter, paginate and order results |
| Response shape (JSON schema snippets) | Helps front‑end devs know exactly what fields exist |
| Error handling conventions | Makes debugging painless |

> ⚠️ *If you’re actually going to ship this API, make sure you comply with all relevant privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA), respect third‑party data licenses, and consider throttling strategies.*

---

### 1️⃣  Base URL & Versioning  

```
https://api.startupstats.com/v1/
```

*All endpoints live under `/v1`. Future major changes get a new prefix (`/v2`).*

---

### 2️⃣  Auth – Bearer Token + Optional Scopes  

```http
GET /v1/startups HTTP/1.1
Host: api.startupstats.com
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Accept: application/vnd.api+json   # optional media type hint
```

Tokens are issued through our OAuth 2.0 flow. You may optionally attach scopes:

| Scope | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `read:startups` | Read access to startup metadata |
| `write:startups` | Create/update/delete startups |
| `analytics:view` | Access aggregated analytics dashboards |

Example scope list returned during consent:

```json
["read:startups", "analytics:view"]
```

---

### 3️⃣  Core Resources  

#### 3.1  `/startups` – List/Search  

| Param | Type | Description |
|------|-----|-------------|
| `q` | string | Free‑text search across name, tagline, industry |
| `industry` | array<string> | Filter by one or more industries |
| `location` | object `{lat:number,lng:number,radius_km:number}` | Geo‑filter within radius |
| `founded_after` | ISO8601 date | Only companies founded after this date |
| `min_funding_usd` | integer | Minimum total funding amount |
| `max_valuation_usd` | integer | Maximum valuation cap |
| `page` | int | Page index (default 1) |
| `per_page` | int | Items per page (max 100) |
| `sort_by` | enum(`name`,`created_at`,`total_funding_usd`) | Order of results |
| `order` | enum(`asc`,`desc`) | Ascending/descending |

##### Example Request

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer abc123" \
"https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?q=lifestyle&industry[]=Health%20Tech&page=2&per_page=25"
```

##### Sample Response

```json
{
  "_meta": {
      "current_page": 2,
      "per_page": 25,
      "total_pages": 12,
      "total_items": 300
  },
  "data":[
      {
          "id":"stp-00123",
          "slug":"fitbit-healthtech",
          "name":"FitBit HealthTech Inc.",
          "tagline":"Wearable health monitoring solutions",
          "description":"...",
          "website_url":"https://www.fitbitht.com",
          "logo_url":"https://cdn.startupstats.com/logos/stp-00123.png",
          "founders":[{"name":"Jane Doe","linkedin":"..."}],
          "headquarters":{"city":"San Francisco","state":"CA"},
          "industries":["Healthcare","IoT"],
          "founded_on":"2018-04-15",
          "employees_range":"51–200",
          "status":"operational",
          "metrics":{
              "total_funding_usd":12500000,
              "last_round_type":"Series B",
              "last_round_amount_usd":5000000,
              "last_round_date":"2023-07-01",
              "valuation_usd":75000000,
              "revenue_last_year_usd":12000000,
              "growth_rate_pct_yoy":35
          }
      },
      ...
  ]
}
```

#### 3.2  `/startups/:id` – Retrieve One Company  

```http
GET https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups/stp-00123
```

Response contains full nested objects: founders, investors, milestones, press releases, financial statements, ESG scores, etc.

#### 3.3  `/investments` – Funding Rounds  

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `round_id` | string | Unique ID |
| `company_id` | string | FK to `/startups` |
| `amount_usd` | decimal | Total capital raised in round |
| `currency` | string | ISO4217 currency code |
| `date_closed` | datetime | When the round closed |
| `lead_investor_ids[]` | array<string> | Investor IDs |
| `series_name` | string | Series A/B/C/D/E/F… |
| `notes` | text | Any extra context |

Pagination works same way as `/startups`.

#### 3.4  `/valuations` – Historical Valuation Snapshots  

Useful for trend charts. Fields include `snapshot_date`, `pre_money_val_usd`, `post_money_val_usd`, `source` (“VC firm”, “IPO filing”).

---

### 4️⃣  Analytics Endpoints (Read‑Only)

These aggregate over many startups and return time series or cohort summaries.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|--------|
| `/analytics/top-funders` | Top N VC firms by total invested USD |
| `/analytics/fundraising-trends` | Monthly fundraising volume globally |
| `/analytics/employment-growth` | Average employee headcount growth rates by region |
| `/analytics/income-stats` | Revenue distribution buckets |

Typical payload:

```json
{
  "metric":"total_funded_usd",
  "time_series":[
      {"month":"2023-01","value":450000000},
      {"month":"2023-02","value":470000000},
      …
  ],
  "cohort_analysis":[
      {"region":"North America","average_growth_percent":28},
      {"region":"Europe","average_growth_percent":22}
  ]
}
```

---

### 5️⃣  Pagination & Filtering Tips  

| Feature | How to Use |
|---------|------------|
| Cursor-based paging | Prefered for high‑volume lists. Return `_links.next_cursor` instead of numeric pages. |
| Server-side filtering | Always apply filters first to reduce bandwidth. |
| ETag caching | Include `ETag` header in responses; client sends `If-None-Match` to avoid re‑downloads. |
| Webhook notifications | Subscribe to events (`new_startup_added`, `funding_announced`) via `/webhooks/register`. |

---

### 6️⃣  Error Handling Conventions  

| Status Code | Body | Explanation |
|-------------|------|--------------|
| `400 Bad Request` | `{error:"invalid_parameter",message:"'page' must be >0"}` | Client error |
| `401 Unauthorized` | `{error:"unauthorized",message:"Missing or invalid token."}` | Wrong/missing auth |
| `403 Forbidden` | `{error:"forbidden",message:"Scope missing."}` | Insufficient permissions |
| `404 Not Found` | `{error:"not_found",message:"No startup matches id stp-99999."}` | Resource absent |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | `{error:"rate_limit_exceeded",retry_after_seconds:60}` | Throttle limit hit |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | `{error:"internal_error",message:"Unexpected failure."}` | Unexpected backend issue |

Clients should implement exponential backoff for transient errors (`429`, `503`).

---

### 7️⃣  SDK Snippets (Python, JavaScript, Go)

#### 7a. Python (Requests)

```python
import requests

BASE_URL="https://api.startupstats.com/v1"

def get_startups(query=None):
    url=f"{BASE_URL}/startups"
    headers={"Authorization":"Bearer YOURTOKEN"}
    params={}
    if query:
        params.update({"q":query,"limit":50})
    r=requests.get(url,headers=headers,params=params)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

print(get_startups("fintech"))
```

#### 7b. Node.js (Axios)

```js
const axios=require('axios');

async function listStartups() {
  const res=await axios({
    method:'get',
    url:'https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups',
    headers:{ Authorization:`Bearer ${process.env.TOKEN}` },
    params:{ q:'health', per_page:30 }
  });
  console.log(res.data);
}

listStartups();
```

#### 7c. Golang (net/http)

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

func main(){
	req,_:=http.NewRequest("GET","https://api.startupstats.com/v1/startups?q=ai",nil)
	req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer MYTOKEN")
	client := &http.Client{}
	resp,err:=client.Do(req)
	if err!=nil{panic(err)}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var result map[string]interface{}
	json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&result)
	fmt.Println(result)
}
```

---

### 8️⃣  Building Your Own Dataset (if you don’t want to pay for a commercial feed)

| Source | Method | Caveat |
|--------|--------|--------|
| CrunchBase Public API | REST | Limited free tier (10k queries/month) |
| AngelList API | OAuth | Requires developer account |
| SEC EDGAR filings | RSS/XML | For IPOs, M&A disclosures |
| LinkedIn Companies API | GraphQL | Restricted to partner apps |
| Twitter Streaming API | Real‑time tweets | Need keyword filters |
| Google News Custom Search | JSON | Paid beyond 100 searches/day |

Combine them into a nightly ETL pipeline (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster) → store in PostgreSQL/PostGIS → expose via FastAPI/GraphQL.

---

### 9️⃣  Legal & Compliance Checklist  

1. **Data Licensing** – Verify each source allows redistribution.  
2. **Privacy Laws** – GDPR requires opt‑in for personal data; CCPA mandates consumer rights notices.  
3. **Rate Limits** – Respect upstream provider caps to avoid IP bans.  
4. **Audit Trail** – Log all external API calls for traceability.  
5. **Terms of Service** – Embed TOS acceptance UI for end‑users.  

---

### 🔚 Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Section | Link |
|---------|------|
| Full Swagger/OpenAPI spec | https://docs.startupstats.com/api/swagger.yaml |
| Developer portal & onboarding | https://developers.startupstats.com/signup |
| FAQ & Troubleshooting | https://support.startupstats.com/hc/en-us/categories/360002345678-Developer-Faq |
| Community Slack | https://slack.startupstats.com/join |

Feel free to copy/paste the above skeleton into your README.md or Postman collection. Happy coding!
